title: A search replaced by the graph's call-site answer shows every line grep prints, or says how many it left out
actual: use_lines() takes the lines `devkb uses --json` returns, which caps the hits per search and leaves out the definition line; the deny answer then says 'devkb answered this search from the graph (Complete)' and lists only those. In the fixture grep prints 8 lines (def line, docstring line, 6 callers); the replacement shows 3 callers and no 'N more' note. Lines are also whitespace-stripped and cut at 110 characters.
expected: A replacement contains every line grep would print (SPEC-DKB-007 R6, 'never collapsed'), or the hook does not replace (alongside / pass-through) when the graph's hit list is truncated (`omitted`/`showing 3 of 5`).
why_it_matters: The agent is told the answer is Complete and that grep's output is superseded; it will conclude there are only 3 callers and miss the others, so a refactor can silently skip call sites.

title: A replaced `grep NAME` does not drop lines where NAME is part of a longer identifier
actual: `grep -rn helper pkg` (substring match) is denied and answered from `uses helper`, a whole-word match: the line `def helper_two(x):` that grep prints is missing from the answer that claims to be Complete.
expected: Either the replacement carries the substring matches grep prints, or a non -w search is not replaced by a whole-word answer.
why_it_matters: Same class as above: the agent trusts the replacement as grep's result and does not see related identifiers (helper_two) the search was meant to reveal.

title: A replacement honours a trailing `| head -N` / `| tail -N` instead of returning every line
actual: `grep -rn helper pkg | head -1` is denied and answered with all 3 call-site lines (is_trim_stage lets trim stages pass as if they changed nothing); `| tail -1` likewise returns the other lines, not the last one. The Grep tool's head_limit is ignored the same way.
expected: The answer is never larger than the command's own output (SPEC-DKB-007 R5): apply the trim or pass the search through.
why_it_matters: The agent asked for one line to keep its context small and is given more, in a call that replaced the command; for `tail` the answer is also the wrong lines.

title: A 'where is X defined' search with no -A/-B/-C is answered with the location line, not the whole body
actual: `grep -rn "def helper" pkg` (intent locate) is denied with the location plus the full body (up to 80 lines): 1175 characters for a 25-character grep output. The spec's own table lists 'where X is defined -> location and body' as 'same, larger than asked'.
expected: locate -> `file:line: signature`, one line per definition (SPEC-DKB-007 §3.3); the body only for read-body (context lines).
why_it_matters: Every definition lookup pays for a body the agent did not ask for, which is the cost SPEC-DKB-007 set out to remove (R5).

title: A `grep -A10 'def f'` on a function longer than 80 lines is not denied with an answer that has none of the 10 lines
actual: For a 122-line function, `grep -n "def big" -A10 pkg/a.py` is denied and the answer is the location and '(Body not shown: big is longer than 80 lines...)'. The 10 lines requested are hidden; the agent must repeat the search. Seen on replayed search #14 (`-A30` on `extract`).
expected: When the body is not shown, do not deny (let grep run), or give at least the lines grep's context would print.
why_it_matters: A denial that carries less than grep prints costs a wasted round trip and a model call each time.

title: A definition search confined to one file gets that file's body when the name is defined in several files
actual: `devkb symbol NAME --source` puts the body on the first match only; after the scope filter the one remaining definition may be a later match with no `source`, and definition_answer reports 'Body not shown: twin is its end is not known' although the function is 3 lines with an exact range. With two files defining `twin`, the search in pkg/b.py is denied with no body, the one in pkg/a.py gets it. The message is also ungrammatical ('twin is its end is not known'). Replayed #664 (`def _read -A4 devkb/process_api.py`) shows it on this repository.
expected: The body of the definition inside the searched file, whichever match it is; the reason text matches the cause.
why_it_matters: The denial hides lines grep would print, with a false reason, whenever a name is defined twice in the repository (common: _read, main, setUp).

title: A `grep '^class '` / `'^def '` listing gets only the symbols of that kind, not the whole outline
actual: `grep -n "^class " pkg/m.py` (prints 2 lines) gets an alongside outline of 7 symbols: classes, methods and functions; replayed `grep -n "^def \|^class " cpp_symbols.py` gets constants and fields too. Also the outline is read with the default limit of 200 symbols and `omitted` is ignored.
expected: The answer lists the kinds the pattern names (and at top level when anchored with ^), or nothing.
why_it_matters: The answer is to a different question and larger than grep's output (R5, R8); it costs tokens on every listing.

title: A search for the word 'async', 'static', 'public' or 'function' as text is not answered with the file's outline
actual: classify() calls any pattern made only of language keywords list-symbols, anchored or not: `grep -n "async" pkg/m.py` (prints the import line and a comment) is answered alongside with the outline of every function in the file.
expected: Only a definition-listing pattern (`^def `, `def `, `class ` with its trailing space or anchor) is a listing; a bare keyword is a literal and gets no answer (R2).
why_it_matters: An answer to a different question, added next to every keyword search.

title: devkb guardrail-stats counts outline-on-open decisions
actual: The hook logs action 'outline-on-open' for the first read of a code file (D2), but ACTIONS lacks it: the logged decision is counted as 'substitute 0, ... repeat 0' and its column is missing from the intent table, though the header says '1 guardrail decision'. Same defect as #188, left for the newest action.
expected: Every action found in the log is counted (#188: 'counts every action it finds').
why_it_matters: The stats are the evidence for the D2 experiment; the decisions it makes are invisible in them.

title: A single-file `grep -n` with a pipe, a redirection or a leading `cd` is logged as a graph miss
actual: single_bash_file() returns None for any command word that is only punctuation (`|`, `2>&1`, `2>/dev/null`) and for a command starting with `cd dir &&`. grep's `line:text` output then has no file name, parse_grep sees no code file and records nothing: all four forms found code in lib/x.rb and logged 0 graph-miss lines, where the plain form logs.
expected: #137: a miss is logged when grep searches a single file, whatever pipe/redirect/cd the agent adds.
why_it_matters: `| head`, `2>&1` and `cd` are how agents usually write such searches, so the misses devkb most needs to learn from are dropped.

title: A graph miss names the enclosing C/C++ function when its opening brace is on its own line
actual: The text scan in enclosing() walks up to the first unindented line; for `int Foo::bar(int x)` followed by `{` on the next line it stops at `{`, finds no function header and returns '' (also for an inline method in a struct). Used whenever the file is not in the graph or changed since the build.
why_it_matters: The ticket draft says 'in ``' for brace-on-next-line code (GNU/Allman style, common in C), so the miss cannot be acted on.

title: The 'Next time ask devkb directly' command works from the directory the search ran in
actual: teach_command() always writes `--project .`. When the agent's cwd is a subdirectory (`cwd=pkg`), the suggested `devkb uses helper --project .` fails with 'no devkb graph at .../pkg/.devkb'.
expected: A command that runs where the agent is: `--project <repo>` or a path relative to the search directory (the D1 teach line is on by default since #267).
why_it_matters: The agent follows the hint, gets an error, and learns that devkb does not work: the opposite of the measured direct-use gain D1 relies on.
